key_insight: PhysStream enables video generation with physics-aware, fine-grained control while generating frames autoregressively, rather than requiring all motion instructions up front. Its structured scene memory helps maintain coherent dynamics and object interactions over time.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the limitation of current controllable video generation methods that either need the full control schedule before generation begins or rely on pixel-space controls that specify object positions instead of true physical behavior.
method: Uses an autoregressive image-to-video generation framework for streaming synthesis.
Introduces structured scene memory to retain and update physics-relevant scene state across frames.
Supports fine-grained motion control grounded in physical dynamics instead of only spatial placement.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it makes interactive video generation more practical, flexible, and physically consistent. It can improve workflows in simulation, content creation, and controllable generative modeling where mid-generation adjustments are important.

paper_title: PhysStream: Streaming Physics-Grounded Video Generation with Structured Scene Memory and Fine-Grained Motion Control
paper_authors: Chuhao Chen, Peter Wonka, Chaoyang Wang, Chen Wang, Qiao Feng
